deep.reconstruction:
Setting: π̂ is the profinite fundamental group of P^1 − {0,1,∞}, free on l_0, l_1, l_∞ with l_∞ l_1 l_0 = 1. Aut_loc(π̂) is the group of automorphisms u that send each inertia generator l_i to a conjugate of l_{σ(i)}^p, for some permutation σ ∈ S_3 and some p ∈ Ẑ^*.

The previous page defines a 'rigidified' group SÊ̂ whose elements are systems ũ = (p, σ, g_0, g_1, g_∞). Such a system determines u by u(l_i) = int(g_i)(l_{σ(i)}^p). The conjugating elements g_i are recorded as data, and each is determined only up to right multiplication by the centralizer of l_{σ(i)}, which is the procyclic group ⟨l_{σ(i)}⟩ ≅ Ẑ. The projection SÊ̂ → Aut_loc(π̂) therefore has kernel i({1} × Ẑ^3), and i : π̂ × Ẑ^{0,1,∞} → SÊ̂ is given by i(g; α) = (1, 1, g l_0^{α_0}, g l_1^{α_1}, g l_∞^{α_∞}).

The composition law (8) is ũũ' = (pp', σσ', u(g'_i) g_{σ'(i)}).

This page does four things.
(i) Grothendieck remarks that (8) is not fully explicit. It involves u(g'_i), which can be computed from the data only when g'_i is given as a word in l_0, l_1, l_∞, or as a limit of such words.
(ii) He computes left multiplication by an element of the 'inner' part (formula 9): i(g; α)·(p, σ, g_i) = (p, σ, g g_i l_{σ i}^{α_{σ i}}). For σ = 1 this specializes to (9').
(iii) He computes the conjugation action of SÊ̂ on the normal subgroup i(π̂ × Ẑ^3) (formula 10): ũ i(g; α) ũ^{-1} = i(u(g); p α_{σ^{-1}0}, p α_{σ^{-1}1}, p α_{σ^{-1}∞}). Thus the twist part Ẑ^3 is acted on through the character p and the permutation σ.
(iv) He repeats that (10) is explicit only when g is given as a (limit of) word(s).

Purpose: this is bookkeeping for the next page. There he restricts to the preimage SE of the discrete group Γ (S_3 times a finite cyclic group) and seeks a partial section Γ^±_p → SE that lifts the elements ρ, σ_i, τ_i. In modern terms SÊ̂ is an extension of Aut_loc(π̂) by Ẑ^3 of 'twists at the three punctures'. Equivalently, it is the automorphism group of π̂ together with chosen paths to the three tangential base points / inertia rigidifications. It is the profinite analogue of the mapping class group of a sphere with three boundary components (boundary Dehn twists) mapping onto the version with punctures.
errors: (9') writes σ in the output tuple although σ = 1 has been substituted; it should read (p, 1, ...). This is a harmless slip.
Formula (10) writes i(Π × Z^{0,1,∞}) without hats; profinite π̂ × Ẑ^3 is intended.

Checks: (8), (9) and (10) are all correct with the definition u(l_i) = int(g_i) l_{σ(i)}^p. In particular, ũ i(g; α) = (p, σ, u(g) g_i l_{σ i}^{p α_i}). Matching this against (9) gives β_{σ i} = p α_i, i.e. β_j = p α_{σ^{-1} j}, as stated.
i is injective because distinct procyclic subgroups ⟨l_i⟩ of the free profinite group intersect trivially. This is implicit but true.

ideas.what: Extension of the group of local (inertia-preserving up to permutation and power) automorphisms of π̂_{0,3} by Ẑ^3, obtained by recording conjugators g_i; explicit multiplication law
ideas.modern_name: automorphisms of the fundamental groupoid with tangential base points / 'special' or rigidified outer automorphisms; boundary-twist extension (cf. braid/mapping class groups with boundary)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Ihara (special automorphisms of free pro-l groups, mid-1980s), Deligne (tangential base points, 1989), Drinfeld (1990), Nakamura and Schneps (1990s)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme discusses the Teichmüller tower and Ĝ acting on π̂_{0,3}, but not this explicit Ẑ^3-extension calculus as far as I know

ideas.what: Formula for conjugation action on the twist subgroup Ẑ^3 via the cyclotomic-type character p and the permutation σ
ideas.modern_name: action of GT / Gal(Q̄/Q) on inertia (twist) generators via cyclotomic character

missed.claim: Grothendieck sets up, in 1981, an explicit coordinate description of a Ẑ^3-extension of Aut_loc(π̂_{0,3}) recording tangential conjugators. This is a 'boundary twist' rigidification predating Ihara's, Deligne's and Drinfeld's formalisms. It is computational groundwork rather than a new result.
missed.quote: l'opération de Ê̂ sur i(π̂ × Ẑ^{0,1,∞}) par automorphismes int. s'explicite aisément, et ne dépend que de u
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is of historical interest only, as evidence of how early Grothendieck worked with rigidified (tangential) data for π_{0,3}. The mathematics is now standard.

deep.surprise_reason: These are correct but routine group-theoretic computations in a semidirect/extension structure whose modern counterparts (tangential base points, GT, boundary twists) are well established. There is only mild historical interest in the early date.
transcription_corrections: In (10), 'ρα_{σ^{-1}0}' etc. should read 'p α_{σ^{-1}0}': the multiplier is the element p ∈ Ẑ^*, not ρ.
In (9') the first argument on the left reads (p, 1, g_0, g_1, g_∞), and the right side as written by Grothendieck has σ (a slip for 1).
'l'opération de Ê̂ sur i(Π × Z^{0,1,∞})' should be understood as i(π̂ × Ẑ^{0,1,∞}), and the group acting is SÊ̂ (the image shows Ê̂ with hats).
